messages:
incident-bot: Pager 🔔 SEV-2 - inference-runtime: sustained KV cache evictions + quantized model OOMs impacting hosted inference (route: /v1/generate). Pager ID p-23456. Please respond in #eng-oncall.
anne-oc: acked, oncall here. seeing spike in 95p latency on the dashboards, starting triage.
miguel-sre: I'm joining. first glance: KV cache miss rate jumped from ~2% -> 38% around 02:11Z, lots of small sequences from a single tenant cluster.
sophia-eng: adding context: yesterday's model routing change enabled more aggressive batching for small seqs; could be interacting with KV cache TTL/eviction.
anne-oc: can we throttle batching quickly? sophia, can you flip the route to preserve prefix caching and disable aggressive batching for the tenant? if so, do it as a canary on region-us-west1.
sophia-eng: doing canary now. patch:
```
route_config {
  tenant: "tenant-42"
  batching: { max_inflight: 4 -> 2 }
  kv_cache: { enabled: true, ttl_s: 900 }
}
```
applied to canary pool us-west1-canary -> watch.
miguel-sre: tailing logs -> seeing reduced eviction rate in canary after ~20s. 95p latency back down ~400ms from 1.2s for canary traffic.
julia-cs: heads up - we're seeing error spike in customer dashboard. Notified affected accounts (Customer A, B). CS will send an incident notification if we escalate.
anne-oc: good. start routing 20% traffic to canary for tenant-42, keep 80% to stable. if metrics look stable for 5m, ramp.
miguel-sre: ramping to 20% now. metrics: kv eviction -> 12%, 95p latency -> 520ms.
ryan-pm: ping on customer impact: which customers hit hard? julia?
julia-cs: Customer A saw 30% increased error rate, some timeouts. Customer B degraded but not failures. We're prepping a status update to stakeholders.
anne-oc: mitigation note: canary changes reduced OOMs (quant models) by disabling aggressive batching; it's safe to roll to all pools for this tenant while we investigate root cause.
sophia-eng: rolling rollout to all regions for tenant-42 now (manual), will monitor.
miguel-sre: monitoring shows system-wide eviction rate dropping from 38% -> 8% over 3 minutes. quant model OOMs decreased to near-baseline.
anne-oc: nice work. now capturing timeline for post-incident review: need followups on KV cache sizing logic, batching heuristics for small sequences, and quantized model memory regression test coverage.
lina-mgr: assignable action items please — we'll track in the postmortem.
ryan-pm: scheduling postmortem: propose Tue 10:00 AM PT (2026-03-24 17:00 UTC). anyone blocked?
miguel-sre: fine for me. I'll prepare initial timeline and key logs.
sophia-eng: I'll prepare a short repro and the rollout config diffs.
julia-cs: I'll prepare customer impact notes and sent messages.
anne-oc: handoff: I need to step out in 10m. miguel, can you take active pager for the next 4h? I'll stay async on thread for blockers.
miguel-sre: taking over pager. contact: miguel-sre (cell: on profile). I'll escalate to infra if we see regression after rollout.
anne-oc: recorded action items inline:
- A1 (miguel-sre): deep root cause on KV TTL/eviction interplay with sequence-length distribution. due: 2026-03-31
- A2 (sophia-eng): add canary gating and automated rollback for batching config changes. due: 2026-04-07
- A3 (eng-reliability): add regression test for quantized model OOMs under high small-seq load. due: 2026-04-14
- A4 (julia-cs): consolidate customer impact notes and send follow-up email templates. due: 2026-03-25
- A5 (lina-mgr): schedule postmortem (ryan proposed date) and own follow-ups.
ryan-pm: we'll use the postmortem template and link to runbooks. please add any missing items.
miguel-sre: quick note: captured a minimal log extract for the postmortem:
```
2026-03-17T02:11:12Z tenant=tenant-42 seq_len=12 kv_evictions=172
2026-03-17T02:11:13Z model=quant-v2 OOM at alloc=782MB
```
anne-oc: thanks. final ops note: we've set temporary increased KV capacity and locked batching configs for the next 24h to avoid flapping.
miguel-sre: keeping pager until 06:30 UTC, will escalate earlier if trends reverse.
julia-cs: sending interim customer update now: "We're mitigating a performance regression caused by caching and batching interaction. Root cause under investigation, next update in 2 hours." :email:
lina-mgr: thanks team. I'll create the postmortem doc and assign owners to the action items. adding link here once ready.
anne-oc: good handoff. closing the immediate page — moving to post-incident tracking. :white_check_mark:"
